facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against calling the set ready is that the terms creditors rely on most sit in executed documents that are missing: the springing maturity, the guarantor list and the covenant definitions are known only from summaries, and the 2026 reports print no covenant test. Against that, the summaries agree with each other and with the balance sheets, every total tied in the checks, and the company states compliance at year-end, so the figures look reliable and only the legal reading is open. Supplying the eighth amendment to the credit agreement, the indentures and the 2026-07-29 announcement would let the legal and perimeter questions be answered, and a later filing that restates 2026 figures or confirms a sale agreement would require the analyses to be rerun. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: Shareholder returns are the strongest evidence against reading the deleveraging as durable. A new repurchase authority of up to USD 750 million, including USD 306 million left from the earlier programme, was approved on 2026-10-27, the remaining authority fell from USD 382 million to USD 306 million within October, and the implied repurchases would lift pro forma net leverage to 4.00x. The company also says it is exploring a sale of nine regional gaming properties carrying USD 280 million to USD 300 million of annual Adjusted EBITDA, which would remove earnings before any proceeds are applied to debt. A fourth quarter release showing buybacks resuming, or sale terms that do not apply proceeds to debt, would reverse the improvement; sale proceeds applied to debt at or above the current multiple would extend it. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against an adequate-but-reversible reading is that the profile may be better than it looks: free cash flow covers 11.22% of debt, buybacks paused for nine months, the revolver fell by USD 578 million, maturities were pushed to 2031 and 2033, and no extraction or liability management is documented. The reversibility case rests on a USD 750 million authority that the board has not yet fully used and on a ruling risk that has not materialised in Kentucky or Virginia. A fourth quarter release showing no buyback resumption and sale proceeds applied to debt would move the view toward strong; a ruling or tax increase on machines, resumed revolver-funded buybacks, or a failure to refinance the 2028 notes ahead of the springing test would move it toward weak. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C5; calculation C8; calculation C13

facts.label: Company description
facts.text: Churchill Downs operates the Kentucky Derby and Churchill Downs Racetrack, 17 historical racing machine venues in Kentucky, Virginia and New Hampshire, the TwinSpires online horse racing wagering business with United Tote and Exacta technology, and ten wholly owned regional casinos plus two equity-method casino investments, reported in three segments. The model supports cash-flow visibility through a recurring annual event, regulated gaming licences and several revenue lines, but earnings depend on state-granted permission for machines and on the Derby quarter, so debt service capacity is strong in normal conditions and exposed to legal change, and refinancing confidence rests on that legal stability. facts.label: Porter's five forces
facts.text: Competitive rivalry is high: racetracks compete for horses and for simulcast wagering dollars, casinos compete with other gaming and sports betting for discretionary spend, and more states legalising gaming increases supply, which pressures margins and share; this links to lower EBITDA and higher leverage. The threat of new entrants comes from new state authorisations and licences rather than capital, which matters because new gaming near the company's venues could take revenue. Substitutes such as sports wagering and other entertainment compete for the same spend, buyers are individual customers whose discretionary spend can shift, and suppliers matter in two places: horsemen's groups negotiated annually and machine manufacturers that could limit popular games or require participation leases, which can raise costs or reduce machine yield. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The initiating condition is a ruling or tax increase that stops or taxes machines in Kentucky or Virginia, as happened in Louisiana. The first operational break is loss or relocation of machines, which cuts Live and Historical Racing revenue and Adjusted EBITDA, and the financial transmission is lower free cash flow while project capital and the dividend continue; each USD 100 million of lost EBITDA lifts net leverage from 3.94x to 4.31x. # Source readiness for Churchill Downs Inc
## Request

Churchill Downs Inc (issuer id chdn), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. This answer assesses whether the supplied sources can support the selected analyses of Business & governance, Financial foundation and Fundamental credit.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven filings support a credit snapshot of Churchill Downs Incorporated through Q3 2026, but creditors cannot yet verify debt terms, covenant headroom or the effect of the possible sale of nine regional gaming properties. Statements, the debt note, segment results and the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation are present for FY2025 and for each 2026 quarter, and their totals tie. The debt agreements, proxy statement, ratings and market prices are not in the set. Two points need care: the filing's net debt line does not deduct cash, and USD 600 million of 2027 notes was redeemed on 2026-10-19, after the balance sheet date.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C1; calculation C2
### Key findings

Every period the later analyses need is printed in the set: the audited FY2025 year, the three 2026 quarterly reports and the three matching earnings releases, which together give FY2025, nine months 2026 and nine months 2025 for a last-twelve-months build. The latest document is dated 2026-10-28, eight days before the cut-off of 2026-11-05, and nothing in the set is dated after the cut-off, so no later fact enters the analysis.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C8

The reporting entity is Churchill Downs Incorporated, one consolidated registrant, so debt, earnings and cash flow are group figures and no subsidiary perimeter has to be separated. The 2030 senior notes were issued by a wholly owned subsidiary, and the indentures and the credit agreement are described as having guarantors that the supplied text does not name, so the legal obligor and guarantor structure is not established.

Debt evidence is consistent across the debt note, the management discussion table and the balance sheet: total debt was USD 4,748 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 5,155 million at 2025-12-31, and the balance sheet lines reconcile to the debt note at both dates. The fall reflects the September 2026 refinancing, which added a USD 500 million term loan due 2033, moved the revolver and term loan A maturity from July 2029 to September 2031 and repaid the older term loan B-1 and revolver borrowings. The extension carries a springing maturity that applies if notes maturing before 2031-09-25 are not refinanced at least 91 days before they fall due.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C4

USD 600 million of 2027 senior notes was redeemed on 2026-10-19 with revolver borrowings, after the balance sheet date. The September balance sheet shows current maturities of USD 659 million against USD 63 million at year-end, and the supplied text does not itemise those current maturities, so Financial foundation has to carry the redemption as a dated event with its own pro forma line and never blend it into September amounts.

Adjusted EBITDA includes the company's share of equity-investee EBITDA and the portion attributable to noncontrolling interests, and segment revenue is stated before intercompany eliminations, so Q3 2026 revenue of USD 714 million across the three segments reconciles to consolidated net revenue of USD 696 million only after All Other revenue of USD 2 million and USD 20 million of eliminations. Covenant evidence is dated. The annual report prints interest coverage of 3.9x against a required level above 2.5x and a consolidated total secured net leverage ratio of 1.4x against a maximum below 4.0x at 2025-12-31, with a statement that the company complied with all applicable covenants at that date. The 2026 quarterly reports print neither the tests nor a compliance statement, so covenant headroom at 2026-09-30 is not established from the set.

On 2026-07-29 the company announced that it is exploring a sale of nine wholly owned regional gaming properties, which it says represent USD 280 million to USD 300 million of annual Adjusted EBITDA including retail sportsbook and market access. The only statement of this in the set is one sentence in the Q3 2026 quarterly report, and the earlier Q2 documents mention strategic alternatives only in their risk language, so the announcement, the property list, any buyer, price, timetable or use of proceeds are not established. Until they are, the perimeter that Business & governance and Fundamental credit describe stays open.

The debt documents, the proxy statement and any rating or market price are the main absent sources. The annual report lists the indentures, supplemental indentures and credit agreement among its exhibits but they are not supplied, and directors, ownership and compensation are incorporated by reference to a proxy statement that is also absent. Debt terms therefore rest on the filings' own summaries, and legal and covenant analysis cannot be completed from this set.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against calling the set ready is that the terms creditors rely on most sit in executed documents that are missing: the springing maturity, the guarantor list and the covenant definitions are known only from summaries, and the 2026 reports print no covenant test. Against that, the summaries agree with each other and with the balance sheets, every total tied in the checks, and the company states compliance at year-end, so the figures look reliable and only the legal reading is open. Supplying the eighth amendment to the credit agreement, the indentures and the 2026-07-29 announcement would let the legal and perimeter questions be answered, and a later filing that restates 2026 figures or confirms a sale agreement would require the analyses to be rerun.

# Financial foundation for Churchill Downs Inc
## Request

Churchill Downs Inc (issuer id chdn), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. This answer normalises the issuer's financial statements for FY2024, FY2025 and 2026 to 2026-09-30, builds last-twelve-months figures, net debt and leverage and interest-cover metrics, and records the definition conflicts and gaps behind them.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Net debt fell to 3.94x EBITDA at 2026-09-30 from 4.64x at year-end 2025, with higher earnings and cash-funded debt repayment each contributing, but slower buybacks drove the repayment and the new USD 750 million repurchase authority can reverse it.

Net debt was USD 4,555 million at 2026-09-30. Pro forma for the 2026-10-19 redemption of the 2027 notes, which the revolver funded, it is USD 4,555 million and 3.94x, and USD 4,631 million and 4.00x if about USD 76 million of implied October repurchases is added. On the issuer's own Adjusted EBITDA the 2026-09-30 net leverage is 3.66x.
Basis: calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C5; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28
### Key findings

Net debt over EBITDA fell by 0.70x between year-end 2025 and 2026-09-30, using EBITDA for the last twelve months. Higher EBITDA explains 0.38x of the fall and lower net debt explains 0.32x, so the improvement is about as much earnings growth as repayment. On Adjusted EBITDA the same ratio moved from 4.09x to 3.66x, and total debt over EBITDA moved from 4.62x at year-end 2024 to 4.83x at year-end 2025 and 4.08x at 2026-09-30.
Basis: calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6

Net debt fell by USD 374.6 million in the nine months because free cash flow after capital expenditure, cash interest and cash tax was USD 484 million, against dividends of USD 31 million, repurchases of USD 44 million and USD 31 million to buy out a noncontrolling interest. Repurchases were USD 396 million in nine months 2025, so the deleveraging reflects a pause in buybacks, a discretionary choice by the company rather than a structural change in how cash is used. Debt had risen in 2025 as the revolver grew by USD 279.5 million while the company spent USD 427.8 million on repurchases and USD 185.3 million on gaming rights.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 78–79; calculation C7; calculation C8

Cash interest paid fell from USD 306.8 million in FY2024 to USD 294.5 million in FY2025 and USD 274.5 million over the last twelve months, which lifted EBITDA cover from 3.46x to 3.61x and 4.22x, or 4.54x on Adjusted EBITDA. The improvement follows the lower debt balance; the new term loan B due 2033 prices at 175 bp over SOFR, the same margin as the term loan B-1 it replaced.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 79; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C3; calculation C5

Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,245.3 million for the last twelve months is USD 88.1 million above calculated EBITDA of USD 1,157.2 million. Equity-investee earnings sit inside both measures: equity income was USD 139.4 million in FY2025 but only USD 116.0 million, or 83.21%, arrived as distributions, so part of EBITDA is not cash available to creditors. Adjusted EBITDA also adds back the issuer's share of equity-investee interest, depreciation and amortization of USD 38.6 million in FY2025 and USD 47.5 million of impairments.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 77–79; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C3; calculation C11; calculation C12

Liquidity at 2026-09-30 was USD 167 million of cash and USD 1,111 million of undrawn revolver, USD 1,278 million in all. The USD 600 million redemption of the 2027 notes on 2026-10-19 was funded from the revolver, so pro forma undrawn revolver capacity is USD 511 million and cash plus undrawn is USD 678 million, before about USD 76 million of implied repurchases.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C9

After the redemption the next note maturity is USD 700 million of 2028 senior notes due 2028-01-15. The amended revolver and term loan A are due September 2031 but carry a springing maturity if notes due before 2031-09-25 are not refinanced at least 91 days ahead, and if that test covers the 2028 notes it would fall about 2027-10-16. The credit agreement is not supplied, so which notes the test covers is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C13

Principal debt was USD 4,748 million against a carrying value of USD 4,722 million at 2026-09-30, a difference of USD 26 million of unamortized premium and financing costs. The quarterly report's own net debt line of USD 4,063 million is debt net of current maturities and costs, not net of cash, so this module reports net debt after cash of USD 4,555 million. The releases quote net bank leverage of 3.8x without a definition, and principal debt over last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA is 3.81x, which matches at one decimal but is not stated to be the definition.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C14

The annual report states that the 2030 and 2031 senior notes mature on 13 April 2030 and 25 April 2031, but the three 2026 quarterly reports state 1 April 2030 and 1 May 2031. The later dates are used here, the years are unaffected, and the Source readiness listing, which used the annual report's dates, is corrected by this answer.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 111–112; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; Source readiness (CP-0)

Deferred revenue, a non-debt funding float tied to advance receipts for events such as the Kentucky Derby, fell from USD 70 million at year-end 2025 to USD 48 million at 2026-09-30 as the revenue was recognised, which is a working-capital outflow rather than a debt repayment.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C15
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

Shareholder returns are the strongest evidence against reading the deleveraging as durable. A new repurchase authority of up to USD 750 million, including USD 306 million left from the earlier programme, was approved on 2026-10-27, the remaining authority fell from USD 382 million to USD 306 million within October, and the implied repurchases would lift pro forma net leverage to 4.00x. The company also says it is exploring a sale of nine regional gaming properties carrying USD 280 million to USD 300 million of annual Adjusted EBITDA, which would remove earnings before any proceeds are applied to debt. A fourth quarter release showing buybacks resuming, or sale terms that do not apply proceeds to debt, would reverse the improvement; sale proceeds applied to debt at or above the current multiple would extend it.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; calculation C10
### Limitations

The issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is calculated from net income, interest, tax and depreciation and amortization, and the last-twelve-months build combines one-decimal annual amounts with whole-million interim amounts.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C3

The maturity table is the one printed at 2025-12-31 and predates the September 2026 refinancing; the quarterly reports print no later table, and rebuilding one would need amortization schedules that are not stated.
No source states the legal rank of any facility, the revolver availability at 2024-12-31 or covenant results after 2025-12-31, so the debt stack is unranked and covenant headroom is not calculated.

- The legal rank, guarantor scope and cumulative priority of every facility at 2026-09-30 are not stated, which leaves the debt stack unranked and limits any priority or recovery reading; severity High; the action is to supply the credit agreement and the indentures.

- Covenant levels and the issuer's actual ratios are printed only at 2025-12-31, so covenant headroom at 2026-09-30 is not established and is not inferred; severity High; the action is to supply the covenant section of a later filing or a compliance certificate.
- The revolver availability at 2024-12-31 is not stated, so the undrawn facilities for that year are not supplied; severity Low; the action is to read the FY2024 annual report.

- The annual report's net change in cash for FY2024 includes cash flows of discontinued operations that the three activity totals exclude, so the net change in cash for that year is left as not supplied; severity Low; the action is to treat the activity totals as the comparable measure.

- The filings print dashes rather than amounts for All Other revenue in the interim periods, for impairments in nine months 2026 and Q3 2026, for the noncontrolling interest in Q3 2026, for the gain on settlement of a liability, the acquisition of gaming rights and impairments in some cash flow periods, for debt issuance costs in nine months 2025, and for income taxes receivable, income taxes payable and dividends payable on some balance sheet dates; each is left as not supplied rather than read as zero; severity Low.
- The cash flow lines for the acquisition of a noncontrolling interest and for discontinued operations are printed only in some periods, so the other periods are not supplied; severity Low.
- The last-twelve-months revenue of All Other and the 2025-09-30 balance sheet are not available, so those cells of the credit metrics table are not calculable; severity Low.

- The aggregate dividend declared on 2026-10-27 is not stated and the share count at the record date is not stated, so the dividend's effect on net debt is not supplied; severity Medium; the action is to update when the payment is reported.
- The redemption price and accrued interest on the 2027 senior notes are not stated, so a premium or accrued interest paid on 2026-10-19 is not reflected; severity Low.
- The October 2026 repurchases are implied by the change in remaining authority and are not stated directly; severity Medium; the action is to confirm from the fourth quarter report.

- The debt maturity ladder is dated 2025-12-31 and no later table is printed, so the maturity profile after the September 2026 refinancing is not stated; severity Medium; the action is to obtain the amortization schedules.

- The proceeds and repayments of borrowings in nine months 2026 exclude USD 198 million of debt exchanged non-cash in the refinancing, so gross financing flows do not equal the change in debt; severity Low.
- Diluted earnings per share and share counts are kept out of the statement tables, which hold amounts in USD millions only; severity Low.

# Business and governance facts for Churchill Downs Inc
## Request

Churchill Downs Inc (issuer id chdn), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. This answer sets out the business, ownership, governance, capital allocation and transaction facts that matter to creditors and the governance risk they support.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Churchill Downs is a company with no sponsor identified, so creditors depend on board capital-allocation choices, while a seasonal Derby profit pool, legally contingent machine revenue and a possible sale of nine gaming properties make the earnings base less certain than leverage suggests.

The second quarter, which holds Kentucky Derby week, produced 47.80% of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA, historical racing machines in Kentucky and Virginia supplied 33.35% of nine-month revenue, and the company says nine properties carrying USD 280 million to USD 300 million of annual Adjusted EBITDA are under review for sale. Governance risk is Medium because shareholder returns, which reached 92.67% of free cash flow in FY2025, can reverse the 2026 deleveraging, and the evidence on control and legal capacity is incomplete.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ex991pressrelease07-29x26.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C7
### Key findings

No sponsor or controlling holder is identified, so creditors have no equity backstop to rely on and no sponsor extraction pattern to price, and the capital-allocation record is the best evidence of how the board treats lenders. The company is widely held and its filings defer director, ownership and related-party detail to a proxy statement that is not supplied, so the absence of a controlling holder is the reading of the filings rather than a verified fact.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 134; Source readiness (CP-0)

Earnings are concentrated in the quarter that holds Kentucky Derby week. Second-quarter Adjusted EBITDA of USD 477 million was 47.80% of the nine-month total and 38.30% of the last twelve months, and second-quarter revenue was 41.90% of nine-month revenue, so one event week largely decides each year's cash generation, and quarter-end debt readings should be set against last-twelve-months earnings rather than a single quarter.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-04-22_ex991pressrelease04-22x26.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ex991pressrelease07-29x26.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C3

Machine revenue is legally contingent and sits in two states. Historical racing machines produced 33.35% of nine-month revenue, with 52.55% of the machines in Kentucky and 47.45% in Virginia, and the Louisiana Supreme Court's ruling ended the company's machines in Louisiana on 2025-05-08 and sent them mainly to Virginia. In Q3 2026 Central Virginia earnings fell by USD 10 million, including USD 5 million of new tax under a structure effective 2026-07-01 and the effect of competition, so the redeployed capacity is facing a tougher market while one adverse ruling or tax change in either state would cut revenue directly.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C4

Part of Adjusted EBITDA is earnings the company does not control. Equity income inside Gaming Adjusted EBITDA was USD 187.1 million over the last twelve months, 15.02% of the total and 37.95% of Gaming, while distributions were USD 106 million against equity income of USD 115 million in nine months and the two casino affiliates carry long-term debt of USD 760 million that sits at the affiliate level ahead of the company's equity claim on their cash.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 125; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; calculation C8

Capital returns have been large and discretionary. Repurchases and dividends equalled 92.67% of free cash flow after capital expenditure in FY2025, when the revolver grew while the company bought back stock and acquired Casino Salem for USD 180.0 million, then fell to 15.50% in nine months 2026 as the revolver was repaid. A new repurchase authority of up to USD 750 million was approved on 2026-10-27 and the fall in remaining authority from USD 382 million to USD 306 million implies USD 76 million of October repurchases, which would add to net debt after the redemption, so deleveraging can reverse by board decision.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation C7; calculation C10

The possible sale of nine wholly owned regional gaming properties would remove 22.48% to 24.09% of last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA, yet the quarterly report states it in one sentence and gives no buyer, price, timetable or use of proceeds, and it does not say which of the ten listed wholly owned properties stays. Creditors gain only if proceeds repay debt at a multiple at least equal to the leverage left behind, so the perimeter stays open until terms are disclosed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation C5

The October 2026 redemption of the USD 600 million 2027 notes with revolver borrowings lifts the secured share of principal from 34.71% to 47.35%. The credit agreement is collateralized by substantially all wholly owned assets and the remaining notes are described as unsecured, so the 2028, 2030 and 2031 notes sit behind more secured debt, although no source states legal rank.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 69; calculation C6

Reporting quality is a genuine strength. The financial statements and internal control over financial reporting were audited by PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, management concluded that internal control was effective at 2025-12-31, and results are released quarterly, although covenant ratios and a compliance statement appear only in the annual report and a new financial reporting system was introduced in 2026.

Large builds absorb cash before they earn. The company plans a first-turn building of USD 280 million to USD 300 million at Churchill Downs Racetrack due by the 2028 Derby and Rockingham Grand Casino of USD 180 million to USD 200 million opening in mid-2027, while 2026 project capital was cut by USD 30 million at the midpoint to a plan of USD 160 million to USD 180 million, so the programme competes with debt repayment and buybacks for free cash flow through 2028.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 66; EX-99.1_2026-04-22_ex991pressrelease04-22x26.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation C12
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The best evidence for lower governance risk is the record: audited reporting, an effective control report, no documented extraction, cure request or liability management, a dividend that has risen for sixteen consecutive years at a small cash cost, and buybacks that paused while the revolver fell by USD 578 million in 2026. The supplied legal proceedings disclosure describes only ordinary routine litigation, with no pending ruling against machines in Kentucky or Virginia. A proxy statement showing a controlling holder or related-party arrangements, or buybacks resuming with revolver funding, would raise the risk level, while sale proceeds applied to debt and a defined perimeter would lower it.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 128; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 132; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C7; calculation C11
### Limitations

- Because the proxy statement is not supplied, the finding that no sponsor or controlling holder exists rests on the annual report cover and its deferral of ownership detail, and a disclosed large holder would turn the governance reading from capital-allocation discipline into a control question.

- The sale exploration is described by one sentence, so the perimeter view cannot say which properties would leave or whether proceeds reduce debt, and a signed sale agreement would replace the open perimeter with a defined one.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32

- The credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so legal capacity for distributions, asset sales and priming is separated from willingness only by documented behaviour, and the Medium risk level would move if the baskets prove tight or wide.
- Segment and affiliate shares follow the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA definition, which includes affiliate earnings, so the profit mix between racing and casinos would shift if affiliates were excluded.
- The business description and machine counts come from the annual report filed on 2026-02-25, so venue totals may have moved since, which would change the machine concentration shares only slightly.
### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The company issued no new notes in 2026 and entered one new debt instrument, a USD 500 million term loan B due 2033 issued at 99.875% of principal at 175 bp over SOFR on 2026-09-25, alongside an eighth amendment that extended the revolver and term loan A to September 2031 with a springing maturity. The proceeds repaid the term loan B-1 and revolver borrowings, so the transaction extended maturities rather than adding debt, and the secured share of principal then rose when the USD 600 million 2027 notes were redeemed with revolver borrowings on 2026-10-19.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C6

Other transactions that matter to creditors are the August 2025 purchase of 90% of Casino Salem for a base price of USD 180.0 million funded with revolver borrowings, the August 2026 re-acquisition of the 49% of United Tote held by the New York Racing Association together with a tote services extension to 2035, and the announced exploration of a sale of nine wholly owned regional gaming properties. The re-acquisition removed a put right and a redeemable noncontrolling interest, while the sale exploration has no stated terms.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C9; calculation C13

# Fundamental credit view of Churchill Downs Inc
## Request

Churchill Downs Inc (issuer id chdn), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. This answer synthesises the source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance work into a fundamental credit view, with the main strength, the primary downside path and the monitoring triggers.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Churchill Downs has an adequate credit profile with leverage falling through 2026, but the improvement is reversible because shareholder returns are discretionary and a third of revenue depends on machine laws in two states.

Net debt was USD 4,555 million at 2026-09-30, or 3.94x last-twelve-months EBITDA; pro forma for the revolver-funded redemption of the 2027 notes on 2026-10-19 it is USD 4,555 million and 3.94x, and USD 4,631 million and 4.00x if about USD 76 million of implied October repurchases is added. Free cash flow after capital expenditure of USD 529.9 million is 11.22% of debt, interest cover is 4.22x and liquidity is USD 678 million pro forma, so near-term liquidity risk is low. The primary downside path is a ruling or tax change on machines, which supply 49.39% of segment earnings, landing on a balance sheet with committed projects and a USD 750 million buyback authority.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C6; calculation C9
### Key findings

Leverage has improved but not yet durably. Net debt over EBITDA fell from 4.64x at year-end 2025 to 3.94x at 2026-09-30 and from 4.09x to 3.66x on Adjusted EBITDA, with higher earnings and repayment contributing about equally, while the new buyback authority and the implied October repurchases show how the 3.94x can become 4.00x within weeks; the quarterly report's own net debt line is not net of cash, so this view uses net debt after cash.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C2

Cash generation is the core strength. Free cash flow after capital expenditure, cash interest and cash tax was USD 529.9 million over the last twelve months, 42.55% of Adjusted EBITDA, while capital expenditure took 18.14% of Adjusted EBITDA and EBITDA covered cash interest 4.22x, so the business can repay debt from internal cash if shareholder returns stay restrained.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3

Liquidity is adequate and the revolver and term loan A run to September 2031. Cash of USD 167 million and undrawn revolver of USD 511 million pro forma for the redemption give USD 678 million against identified near-term cash calls of USD 88.15 million to USD 108.15 million, and scheduled amortization is only USD 60 million a year until the USD 700 million 2028 notes mature in January 2028.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C6; calculation C7

The 2028 notes make 2027 the key financing window. The revolver and term loan A carry a springing maturity if earlier notes are not refinanced at least 91 days ahead, which would be about 2027-10-16 for the 2028 notes if the test covers them; the credit agreement is not supplied, so coverage is not established, and the redemption of the 2027 notes with revolver borrowings means the revolver now carries USD 679 million.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C8

Machine revenue is the primary downside. Historical racing machines supply 33.35% of nine-month revenue and Live and Historical Racing supplies 49.39% of segment Adjusted EBITDA, all in two states, and a Louisiana court ruling already ended the company's machines there; each USD 100 million fall in EBITDA lifts net leverage from 3.94x to 4.31x, so a state-level shock would move leverage well above the current level before management levers apply.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C4; calculation C9

Earnings are seasonal and partly not controlled cash. The Derby quarter produced 47.80% of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA and 38.30% of the last twelve months, and equity-investee earnings are 15.02% of Adjusted EBITDA with 92.17% cash conversion, so Adjusted EBITDA overstates controlled cash and quarter-end debt readings need last-twelve-months earnings.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ex991pressrelease07-29x26.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C9; calculation C11

Financial policy is the main swing factor and the governance risk is Medium. Shareholder returns were 92.67% of free cash flow in FY2025 and 15.50% in nine months 2026, no sponsor is identified so there is no equity backstop, and reporting is audited and quarterly, while the proxy statement and the debt documents are not supplied, so control and legal capacity are not established.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C9

The perimeter and the debt stack are shifting. The company is exploring a sale of nine properties with USD 280 million to USD 300 million of annual Adjusted EBITDA, which would lift net leverage on Adjusted EBITDA from 3.66x to between 4.72x and 4.82x unless proceeds of at least USD 1,024.80 million to USD 1,098.00 million repay debt, and the secured share of principal rises from 34.71% to 47.35% after the redemption, so the remaining notes sit behind more secured debt although legal rank is not stated.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5; calculation C9

Interest-rate exposure rose with the redemption. The company reports that a one percentage point rise in SOFR would cut net income and operating cash flow by USD 12 million on USD 1.6 billion of variable-rate debt, and moving USD 600 million of fixed-rate notes into the revolver lifts that to about USD 16.37 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C10
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against an adequate-but-reversible reading is that the profile may be better than it looks: free cash flow covers 11.22% of debt, buybacks paused for nine months, the revolver fell by USD 578 million, maturities were pushed to 2031 and 2033, and no extraction or liability management is documented. The reversibility case rests on a USD 750 million authority that the board has not yet fully used and on a ruling risk that has not materialised in Kentucky or Virginia. A fourth quarter release showing no buyback resumption and sale proceeds applied to debt would move the view toward strong; a ruling or tax increase on machines, resumed revolver-funded buybacks, or a failure to refinance the 2028 notes ahead of the springing test would move it toward weak.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C5; calculation C8; calculation C13
### Limitations

- Reported EBITDA is calculated by Financial foundation because the issuer states none, so every leverage figure here would be lower on the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA, for example 3.66x against 3.94x for net leverage at 2026-09-30.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1

- The October 2026 repurchases are inferred from the fall in remaining authority and the aggregate dividend is not stated, so the 4.00x pro forma is the upper case and the true figure lies between 3.94x and 4.00x.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation C2

- Legal and covenant terms are not supplied, so whether the springing maturity covers the 2028 notes and how much covenant headroom remains is not established, and the 2027 refinancing date is a conditional one.
- The sale arithmetic is illustrative and not a forecast, because the sources give neither the properties nor the proceeds, so the 4.72x to 4.82x range is a bound on the no-proceeds case.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C5
- No ratings, prices or peers are supplied, so adequate is a judgement from the filings and not a comparison with other leveraged gaming issuers.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strength: the cash engine. Free cash flow after capital expenditure, cash interest and cash tax of USD 529.9 million over the last twelve months covers 11.22% of debt and EBITDA covers cash interest 4.22x, so internal cash can repay debt when buybacks pause, and the pause in 2026 repaid the revolver by USD 578 million.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3; calculation C13

Strength: scale and diversification around a marquee asset. Revenue of USD 3,004.9 million over the last twelve months comes from racing, wagering and ten wholly owned casinos plus two affiliates, with Adjusted EBITDA margin of 41.44%, so a shock to one profit pool other than machines would not overwhelm debt service.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C9; calculation C11

Strength: liquidity and extended maturities. The revolver and term loan A run to September 2031 and a term loan B to 2033, scheduled amortization is USD 60 million a year, and pro forma liquidity is USD 678 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation C6; calculation C7
Strength: reporting quality. Audited statements, an effective control report and quarterly releases give creditors reliable and frequent data.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)

Weakness: legal concentration of machine revenue. A third of revenue and about half of segment earnings depend on machine laws and taxes in Kentucky and Virginia, and the Louisiana ruling shows an adverse outcome is possible, which would raise leverage by 0.37x for each USD 100 million of lost EBITDA.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C4; calculation C9

Weakness: discretionary shareholder returns. Returns reached 92.67% of free cash flow in FY2025 and a new USD 750 million authority exists, so the deleveraging of 2026 can reverse within a quarter, as the implied October repurchases show.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C9; calculation C2

Weakness: perimeter and structure uncertainty. A sale of nine properties with USD 280 million to USD 300 million of Adjusted EBITDA, a rising secured share of debt and unnamed guarantors leave the creditor position undefined until terms and documents are disclosed.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C5
### Company description

Churchill Downs operates the Kentucky Derby and Churchill Downs Racetrack, 17 historical racing machine venues in Kentucky, Virginia and New Hampshire, the TwinSpires online horse racing wagering business with United Tote and Exacta technology, and ten wholly owned regional casinos plus two equity-method casino investments, reported in three segments. The model supports cash-flow visibility through a recurring annual event, regulated gaming licences and several revenue lines, but earnings depend on state-granted permission for machines and on the Derby quarter, so debt service capacity is strong in normal conditions and exposed to legal change, and refinancing confidence rests on that legal stability.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12
### Ownership and group structure

The company is a listed corporation with no sponsor or controlling holder identified, so there is no sponsor equity backstop and no sponsor extraction pattern, and creditor alignment rests on board capital-allocation choices that have swung from heavy buybacks in FY2025 to repayment in 2026. Rivers Casino Des Plaines at 61.3% and Miami Valley Gaming and Racing at 50% are equity-method affiliates with shared consent rights and their own debt of USD 760 million, so their earnings reach the company only as distributions and the guarantor structure of the company's own debt is not named.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 135; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 140
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is discretionary and event-driven: pari-mutuel wagering on live and historical racing, simulcast and online wagering, and casino play, with the Derby quarter supplying 41.90% of nine-month revenue. Machine revenue of 33.35% of revenue and the Virginia tax and competition effect in Q3 2026 show limited pricing power and legal exposure, while wagering services grew only slightly in 2026, so revenue is predictable at the portfolio level but cyclical, discretionary and regulated.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C9
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Costs include taxes and purses, gaming taxes and salaries that move partly with revenue, and fixed property and technology costs, and Adjusted EBITDA margin held between 41.19% and 42.39% from FY2024 to the last twelve months, which shows resilience in a growing period. New tax of USD 5 million for live race days in Virginia from 2026-07-01 shows that tax changes pass directly to margin unless offset elsewhere.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C11
### Capital intensity and FCF conversion

Capital expenditure took 18.14% of Adjusted EBITDA over the last twelve months and free cash flow converted 42.55% of Adjusted EBITDA, with a first-turn building of USD 280 million to USD 300 million due by the 2028 Derby and Rockingham Grand Casino of USD 180 million to USD 200 million due mid-2027 still to be funded. The 2026 project plan was cut to USD 160 million to USD 180 million, which gives flexibility, but seasonality means debt peaks before the Derby cash arrives.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation C3
### Porter's five forces

Competitive rivalry is high: racetracks compete for horses and for simulcast wagering dollars, casinos compete with other gaming and sports betting for discretionary spend, and more states legalising gaming increases supply, which pressures margins and share; this links to lower EBITDA and higher leverage. The threat of new entrants comes from new state authorisations and licences rather than capital, which matters because new gaming near the company's venues could take revenue. Substitutes such as sports wagering and other entertainment compete for the same spend, buyers are individual customers whose discretionary spend can shift, and suppliers matter in two places: horsemen's groups negotiated annually and machine manufacturers that could limit popular games or require participation leases, which can raise costs or reduce machine yield.
### PEST analysis

Political and regulatory factors are a primary credit driver: gaming licences, machine statutes, gaming taxes and sports wagering taxes set the profit pool, and the Louisiana ruling and the Virginia tax structure effective 2026-07-01 are direct evidence. Economic factors matter through consumer confidence and discretionary spending, which the annual report names as a market risk, and interest rates matter through USD 1.6 billion of variable-rate debt. Social and technological factors do not appear to be primary credit drivers based on the provided materials.
### SWOT analysis

Strengths are the Derby asset, free cash flow of USD 529.9 million over the last twelve months, scale across three segments and extended maturities. Weaknesses are machine legal concentration, discretionary buybacks, the 2028 notes and springing maturity, and an Adjusted EBITDA that includes affiliate earnings. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the use of any sale proceeds to repay debt, Rockingham Grand Casino opening in mid-2027, and further revolver repayment. Threats are an adverse ruling or tax change on machines, resumed buybacks funded by the revolver and a failed refinancing of the 2028 notes.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C8
### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and market position are strong on revenue of USD 3,004.9 million, competitive advantage is strong around the Derby and licensed venues, business diversification is average because machines concentrate in two states, cost and capex flexibility is average with a cut project plan, margin stability is average at 41.44% with new Virginia tax, free cash flow stability is average on 42.55% conversion that depends on buybacks, ability to refinance is average with 2028 notes ahead and a springing maturity, liquidity is strong at USD 678 million pro forma, and financial policy and governance is average with a Medium risk level. The trend is improving leverage with reversible drivers, and the missing datapoints are the debt documents, the proxy statement and sale terms.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C6; calculation C11
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are Rockingham Grand Casino opening in mid-2027, the Thoroughbred Championship Series from 2027, extended maturities and the ability to repay the revolver from free cash flow; the headwinds are Virginia tax and competition, the 2028 notes refinancing window by about 2027-10-16, a dividend of about USD 32.15 million payable 2027-01-05 and the repurchase authority. Over three to five years the sector headwind is the legal durability of machine revenue and the tailwind is the completion of the first-turn building by the 2028 Derby, so the outlook for leverage is stable to improving if buybacks stay restrained.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C6; calculation C8
### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is a ruling or tax increase that stops or taxes machines in Kentucky or Virginia, as happened in Louisiana. The first operational break is loss or relocation of machines, which cuts Live and Historical Racing revenue and Adjusted EBITDA, and the financial transmission is lower free cash flow while project capital and the dividend continue; each USD 100 million of lost EBITDA lifts net leverage from 3.94x to 4.31x. Liquidity of USD 678 million pro forma and scheduled amortization of USD 60 million a year mean liquidity distress is unlikely within 12 months, but leverage of about 4.3x would complicate the 2027 refinancing of the 2028 notes ahead of the springing maturity, so management levers are the pause in buybacks, the cut in project capital and asset sales, and the observable triggers are the machine revenue share, the Adjusted EBITDA margin and the revolver draw.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C8
### Overall credit view

Overall, Churchill Downs presents an adequate business profile supported by the Derby asset, scale and free cash flow, but credit quality is constrained by machine legal concentration, discretionary shareholder returns and an unsettled perimeter. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow covers 11.22% of debt, refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the 2028 notes being refinanced before about 2027-10-16 and on the revolver absorbing the redemption, and the primary downside path is a machine ruling or tax change. Further analysis would require the credit agreement, the indentures, the proxy statement and the sale terms. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: legal or tax change on machine revenue.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C3; calculation C8
